GEOMETRY — subordinate only to the product invariants.
Use Image 1 for the product's exact appearance, view and pixel size; the active density branch determines whether its x-y position is fixed or may translate. Apply the product-placement and recomposed-support policy below.
ACTIVE BRANCH: LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE. Choose product x-y freely for usable composition using rigid image-plane translation only; movement is optional. Preserve exact pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never resize, reorient, reproject, or crop the product. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the product; product and support need not move together.

Use LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE placement: translate the laptop horizontally right by about its own width, keeping its current vertical position and every other product invariant. It occupies the right-hand workstation with a clear margin to the frame edge. Independently construct a sturdy rectangular worktable beneath it, with a pale oak top and charcoal metal legs. Leave a broad empty tabletop to the laptop’s left and a continuous floor aisle along the left side of the room. The table’s left end is visible; its right end may extend beyond the frame. Fully support the laptop’s base, with generous clearance behind and beside it and a small working gap at the near edge. Place the working chair directly on the keyboard’s approach axis, pulled back toward the lower right and cropped at the bottom without overlapping the laptop.

Camera: Keep the existing low, gently downward view: the camera is above the tabletop, around seated eye height, with no roll. Preserve the laptop’s exact screen-facing view, visible keyboard deck, perspective and pixel size after its horizontal translation. Construct the table’s long edges rising gently toward the right and its depth edges receding toward the upper left, consistent with the laptop chassis. Glass-wall mullions remain upright, and the furniture and floor share a coherent horizon. The near table edge provides direct keyboard access, with room below and in front for the aligned chair.

Composition: The fully visible laptop sits in the middle plane on the right, unchanged except for one horizontal translation. The pale oak worktable provides full weight-bearing contact, an unobstructed near working edge and an expansive empty area to the left. A charcoal upholstered working chair occupies the near lower-right plane, directly aligned with the keyboard, pulled back sufficiently that its back remains below the laptop silhouette. A broad slate blue felt privacy screen stands on the floor in the far upper-right background, exposing a substantial uninterrupted panel above the laptop. Clear glass walls with slim dark mullions enclose the wide planning room; the left-side aisle remains visibly open on a light gray floor. Cool even daylight enters through the left glazing, with generous fill and gentle shadows. No requested object is omitted; the chair is pulled back and bottom-cropped to reconcile direct working alignment with full product visibility. No people or human reflections appear.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
Determine density from the existing product guide bounds on the current canvas. HIGH-FILL/CLOSE applies when product width or height is at least 45% of the corresponding canvas dimension. LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE applies only when both are below 45%.

In both branches, preserve product identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette proportions, state, finish, details, logo, display content and full visibility.

HIGH-FILL/CLOSE: Preserve the product's exact initial x-y coordinates from the supplied guide. This is unconditional: do not test relocation feasibility and do not move the product even if exact size and all other invariants could be preserved. Drop any user relocation, centering, layout, emphasis, support-edge or composition request that conflicts with this fixed product position. Independently recompose support and room around the fixed product.

LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE: Choose product x-y freely for usable composition using rigid image-plane translation only; movement is optional. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the product; product and support need not move together. Preserve every product invariant. Do not move the product merely to center it or make it more prominent.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Where translation is allowed, if a move cannot preserve every invariant, retain the initial x-y coordinates instead.

For HIGH-FILL/CLOSE, no geometric product change is permitted. For LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE, the only permitted product change is one rigid image-plane x-y translation. Keep its exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, perspective, projection, foreshortening, silhouette, aspect proportions, open/closed and powered state, finish, details, logo and display content. Do not rotate, mirror, resize, shear, warp, reproject, redraw or activate the product. Do not zoom, reframe or change the viewpoint in a way that alters the product.

At the chosen product position, compose a category- and scenario-appropriate support beneath its weight-bearing base. The support may change independently of the product's translation: do not preserve baseline product-to-edge distances, tabletop extents or absolute support-edge locations as requirements. Fully support the base without floating or overhang, with believable front, back and side clearances, natural weight-bearing contact, a contact shadow and material-appropriate reflections on the support.

Construct furniture around the unchanged product orientation. A printer must sit square to its support in 3D with usable access to its operating front. A laptop must face a usable seating or working edge with clear access to its keyboard and display. Do not rotate the product or reveal a different face to fit the furniture. Support axes, room perspective, horizon and vanishing geometry must be compatible with the unchanged product projection at its chosen position; do not retain incompatible geometry from the initial layout.

Keep exactly one product, entirely inside the frame and fully visible. No prop, furniture edge or foreground object may occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product. If the product moves, complete the vacated location as part of the scene. If a candidate placement violates any product or support requirement, choose another placement or recompose the support and room without relaxing the product invariants.

GUIDE LEGEND: Image 1 is the current canvas to edit. Its real product pixels establish the exact product appearance, view and pixel size to preserve. The active density branch determines whether their frame position is fixed or may change by rigid x-y translation. The flat gray region and its boundaries show an initial support plan, not output pixels or required support edges, distances or extents. At the chosen product position, compose an appropriate support beneath the unchanged product. Remove all gray-guide and diagram remnants, any duplicate product and any product-shaped remnant at the initial location. Keep only one intact product at the final location. Render the lighting, palette, materials and textures described here photographically. When blue is unspecified, include one large blue surface/furnishing or multiple clearly visible blue elements whose combined area makes blue immediately noticeable, not a token accent. Tiny props, thin partition frames, screen graphics, sky and lighting casts alone do not qualify. Keep the planned blue materials, visible extent and placement consistent; leave small props neutral by default. Explicit minimal-blue or no-blue requests override that default, as do explicit blue amounts or carriers. Keep the product's original color, finish, exact orientation/view, scale, details and full visibility. HIGH-FILL keeps exact initial x-y; only LOWER-FILL may change x-y by rigid image-plane translation. Never change the product or its camera viewpoint to make room for blue. Retain requested warm-neutral lighting alongside physical blue materials. Do not impose a universal blue hue or coverage percentage. Match soft, uniform exposure and gentle contrast; no bright-hero/dark-room treatment and no orange or global blue color cast. The product pixels in Image 1 control all product details, including any unlit display. Never reproduce any diagram lines, boxes, labels, text or flat guide colors.

Turn Image 1 into a photograph; preserve the laptop's exact orientation/view, pixel size and details; only its x-y position may change. Apply LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE: translate it horizontally right by about its own width, retaining its vertical position and a clear right-frame margin. Preserve identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw/pitch/roll, visible faces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette, proportions, open/powered state, finish, ports, markings and display content. Never mirror, shear, warp, redraw or activate it. Preserve every invariant; never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible; where translation is allowed, retain initial x-y if a move cannot preserve every invariant.

Build a wide glass-walled office planning room around it. Independently construct a sturdy pale oak worktable with charcoal metal legs beneath its entire base. Provide natural contact shadow, ample rear and side clearance and a small gap to the near working edge. Leave broad empty tabletop left of the laptop and an unobstructed floor aisle along the room’s left side. Show the table’s left end; crop its right end if needed.

Keep the low, gently downward, unrolled camera view. Table width edges rise gently right; depth edges recede upper left. Unify furniture, glazing and floor perspective. Place a charcoal working chair near lower right, directly aligned with the keyboard, pulled back and bottom-cropped below the product silhouette. A broad slate blue felt privacy screen stands on the floor in the far upper-right background, exposing a substantial uninterrupted panel above the laptop.

Use cool even daylight from left glazing, generous fill, gentle contrast and realistic wood and fabric texture. Remove diagram marks, gray guide, old shadow and ghosts; finish the vacated area. Exactly one fully visible, unoccluded laptop; no people or human reflections.

One full-bleed photorealistic photograph with natural imperfections; no added text, logos, borders, watermark or CGI look.

Final check before rendering: the product retains its exact identity, orientation/view, visible faces, perspective/foreshortening, scale, silhouette, state and details. HIGH-FILL permits no geometric product change. LOWER-FILL permits only one rigid x-y translation. The support is recomposed beneath the product's chosen position with believable edge clearances, access, full base contact and a plausible contact shadow. The surrounding scene has consistent perspective. The product is fully visible and unoccluded. No product distortion is allowed. Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Where translation is allowed, if a move cannot preserve every invariant, retain the initial x-y coordinates instead. No diagram remnants, old contact shadow, ghost or duplicate product remain.
